title: Quantum Lenia
hook: Paint creatures, then blur their sense of touch with quantum noise.
sub: Lenia is a smooth Game of Life. Every cell feels its neighbours through a ring-shaped kernel. We sent that kernel through a quantum blur on an 18-qubit register. Swap it in and watch Orbium slow down, break up or flood the world.
you_control: Paint the petri dish: drag the pipette to aim and drop an Orbium, brush on random soup, or erase (pointer or keyboard)
Swap the lens: the original kernel or one of three real quantum-blurred kernels (strength 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0), in four kernel shells, and watch Orbi replay the measured fate
Play, pause, step, reset or clear the live dish; set speed, brush size and growth mu / sigma
Seed the dish from a quantum-blurred 528 x 528 snapshot plate (strength 0.25 or 0.5) and see what regrows
qubits_note: Engine-reported ('Recovered N-qubit grid from measurement'). Snapshot: 528 x 528 world, each axis padded to 1024, so 10 + 10 = 20 qubits (the world fills about 27% of the register). Kernel bank: [4, 256, 256], 2 + 8 + 8 = 18 qubits. Not 24: Atlas rejects request bodies over 1 MiB (413, probed for free), so a 2-D world tops out at 20, and results over the platform payload limit fail (TMPRL1103). At reach 0 only the lower qubits of each axis carry rotation (measured from the output support).
honesty: The dynamics are classical Lenia (Chan 2019). Only the kernels and a world snapshot went through blur-core-v1, on Atlas's classical statevector simulator (no QPU). There is no quantum-advantage claim.
